audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer's headline claim is 'he can’t Wind Wall a barrel explosion' — repeated in tldr, winCon, report[0], report[1], report[5], breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0].d. The content layer says the opposite in three places: 'Windwall blocks your Parrrley keg-detonates outright', 'Hold Windwall for your Parrrley keg-detonate to negate the entire barrel chain'. The two layers of the same page contradict each other.
audit.why: Parrrley carries the projectile flag and Wind Wall 'blocks all enemy projectiles for 4 seconds', so a Q thrown into the wall never reaches the keg and nothing detonates. The version that is actually useful is the one neither layer states: Gangplank's basic attack is a melee strike, so detonating the keg with an auto-attack instead of Parrrley is not a projectile and the wall does not stop it.
audit.corrected: tldr and the trade rules rewritten around baiting the wall and melee-detonating; Wind Wall's real 25s-at-rank-1 cooldown and 4s duration added.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 1 and 2 were both scored Gangplank at 8/10 while whys[0] says 'Both are weak at level 1' and whys[1] says 'concede the short trades and farm Parrrley at range'. Levels 4-5 and first item were scored Skill while whys[3] and whys[4] describe them as your takeover and 'your hardest all-in window'. 2+ items was scored Gangplank while whys[6] opens 'Yasuo out-scales you outright'.
audit.why: 55.16% over 1784 games with a hard scaler: you concede level 2, own levels 3 through first item, and lose the late game. The packet chart (Skill, Yasuo, Gangplank, Gangplank, Gangplank, Gangplank, Yasuo) matches the prose.
audit.corrected: Both layers set to the packet chart, ratings rescaled.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[5] and phases[6] were the generic Trinity Force / 'your pattern is at full power' boilerplate, which contradicted the content layer's own account of who spikes when.
audit.why: The first-item stage is your peak because Sheen bursts through one Wind Wall before his crit exists; the two-item stage is his because crit plus Wind Wall plus Sweeping Blade inverts it. Neither was stated in the full layer.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every cooldown line in the full layer says 'track Sweeping Blade' as if it were a punishable window.
audit.why: Sweeping Blade's cooldown is 0.5s at rank 1 and 0.1s at rank 5 — it is never down. The punishable cooldown in this lane is Wind Wall at 25/23/21/19/17s, and the page pointed the player at the wrong one.
audit.corrected: dosFull[0].d rewritten to say deny dash targets rather than wait out E; Wind Wall's cooldown put on dosFull[2].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: The don'ts titles ('Get EQ knocked up', 'Stand on your own barrels', 'Get caught with no escape') had details copied from unrelated matchups.
audit.why: None of the three explained the mistake in its own title. The real mechanics — two Steel Tempest stacks producing the whirlwind knockup, Sweeping Blade being able to dash off any unit including your own keg, and Last Breath blinking 1400 units to any airborne target — were nowhere on the page.
audit.corrected: All three details rewritten from Riot's ability text.

notes: Two things the user should know. (1) The kit file gives Gangplank's PASSIVE a 'projectile' flag while Riot's own description calls it a 'melee strike' — per the standing rule I trusted the description and treated his basic attack as melee, which is what makes melee keg-detonation a real answer to Wind Wall. (2) Gangplank's R also carries the projectile flag; whether Wind Wall blocks Cannon Barrage's falling shots is not answerable from the kit text, so I made no claim about it either way and left the level-6 content untouched.
